title: Reduction comparison for completed constant perfect complexes
statement: Let X be any scheme, A a commutative ring in the coefficient universe, J an ideal, U an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale model site, and n a natural number. Let L:D(A) to D(A/J^(n+1)) be any left adjoint to the actual exact derived restriction of scalars in the small algebraic localization. For a cochain complex P of finite projective A-modules supported in a finite interval, the actual slice derived reduction of adicResidueConstantPerfect(X,J,P) is isomorphic to c_(U,n)(L(Q(P))), where c_(U,n) is [def-sfb-adic-residue-algebra-tower]. No completeness or Noetherian assumption is imposed on A or X.

proof.text: Represent the input P by itself. Its bounded projective terms are flat, so P is K-flat. Exact constant module realization preserves the finite-free retractions of its finite projective terms, and hence flatness. Its bounded support gives a K-flat sheaf complex. Algebraic derived scalar extension, completed coefficient extension, and finite reduction can therefore all be computed termwise on these complexes. Reuse model_kflat and constantPresentationIso from AdicPerfectModelCompleteReduction, identifying the strict-perfect constant realization with the commutative module-sheafification presentation.

The composite of the actual coefficient map with the n-th projection is the ordinary quotient map by limit.lift_π. Reuse scalarChangeCompTo to balance successive extensions and constantChangeIso plus complexComparison to identify direct extension with constant realization of algebraic scalar extension. Componentwise moduleComparison_tensor makes complexComparison invertible. Apply changeOverComplexIso to obtain the same chain isomorphism after actual slice restriction.

The K-flat computation of ConstantCompletion.derivedExtension identifies the actual local derived reduction with the localization of this chain isomorphism. The algebraic moduleDerivedAdjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints identify the supplied L with moduleDerivedExtension. Its moduleRepresentative on bounded projective P is invertible by categorical bounded-flat K-flatness. Apply the exact constant functor and exact slice localization, use their mapDerivedCategoryFactors, and compose the resulting isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem adicResidue_perfect_reduction_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A]
    (J : Ideal A) (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X) (n : ℕ)
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} (A ⧸ J ^ (n + 1))))
    (_adj : L ⊣ DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction J n)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A) ℤ) (c d : ℤ)
    (_hc : P.IsStrictlyGE c) (_hd : P.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (_hP : ∀ q : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X q) ∧ Module.Projective A (P.X q)) :
    Nonempty
      ((adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U n).obj
        ((adicResidueRestriction
          (CategoryTheory.ConstantCompletion.completed
            (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J) U).obj
              (adicResidueConstantPerfect X J P)) ≅
        (adicResidueFiniteConstant.{u, v} X J U n).obj
          (L.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)))
